title: Duchy of Prussia
capsule: The Duchy of Prussia was created in 1525 when Grand Master Albert of Brandenburg-Ansbach secularized the Teutonic Order's Baltic territory under Lutheran principles and received it as a hereditary fief from Polish King Sigismund I through the Prussian Homage, making it the first Protestant state in history. Albert founded the Albertina University at Königsberg in 1544 and established a Lutheran church structure; his son Albert Frederick (1568–1618) became mentally incapacitated, bringing the duchy under Brandenburg regency and leading to the Great Elector's eventual sovereignty. Frederick William secured full independence through the Treaty of Wehlau in 1657, and in 1701 Elector Frederick III crowned himself King Frederick I of Prussia, elevating the duchy into a kingdom.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The Duchy of Prussia's territory is very well attested from Teutonic Order administrative records and Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth documentation; borders are among the more precisely defined of early-modern European principalities.
